name: high-key-white-monolith
prompt: Tall portrait photograph of a boundless white infinity cove, floor sweeping up into the back wall in one soft curve so there is no corner and no horizon, bathed in even, wraparound softbox light from every direction: no cast shadows, only a pale contact shadow under each trainer. In the exact middle of the frame rises one towering slab of stacked office paper, crisp and rectangular as a plinth of white marble, its edges showing thousands of fine sheet lines, its top nearly touching the upper edge of the picture. At its foot sits a small gallery wall card printed with THE RULES in neat black sans-serif capitals. Lined up in front of it, tiny against the slab, stand four people in a tidy row, bodies turned three-quarters away from us, heads tipped back to stare up its height. Each wears a bright hand-knitted balaclava in its own loud colour, hot pink, lime green, cobalt blue, tangerine, the knit closed over the whole face, solid wool where eyes, nose and mouth would be. The person second from the right has turned to look back at the lens, showing the mask front: a wide white knitted ring outlining the face, and inside it, high up toward the upper right of the picture, a small red triangle with rounded corners stitched over the wearer's left eye, never in the centre. The others show the edge of the same red triangle on their turned heads. Plain, current UK clothing in black and slate grey: zip hoodie, bomber jacket, puffer gilet, joggers, white-soled trainers; the knit tucked into every collar; black gloves on all hands, sleeves pulled over the wrists, no bare skin anywhere. Shot from far back at chest height on a long lens, perfectly level and mirror-symmetrical, motionless and calm. Colour: white on white with faint silver-grey tones; the knitted masks and their red triangles are the only saturated colour in the picture. Hushed, clean, exhibition-quiet, high-key.
